<reason>B more convincingly distinguished a primary economic benchmark from an exclusive measure of governmental success. A's argument about headline incentives remained relevant, but repeatedly treated GDP's omissions as zero policy weight despite B's binding-standards alternative. B also exposed unresolved distributional and forecasting choices in A's satisfaction headline. A's closing defended democratic contestation without establishing that replacement would make accountability firmer. B answered the pressure more directly and better explained why welfare outcomes could remain enforceable without displacing GDP.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's strongest reply distinguished individuals weighting aspects of their own lives from government weighting different people: average satisfaction can improve while the low-well-being group grows. This directly undercut A's claim that respondents' own judgments eliminate political discretion over the headline.</best_rebuttal>
